gen-dafont-dogica-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Dogica stretches its letters wide, with a lowercase that nearly climbs to capital height and a gap at every curve's end. Mochiy Pop One follows with the stencil-cut look of laser-cut sheet.
gen-dafont-dogica-instrument-sans: Dogica arrives heavy and wide, almost shouting. It owns the big, punchy moments, while Instrument Sans handles the quiet work, its stroke weight never wavering and its curves staying tidy.
gen-dafont-dogica-mulish: Approachable is the first word for Mulish, with its large x-height and strokes that never swell or thin. And Dogica supplies the weight above it, wide-set and commanding, so the page has both a loud voice and an easy one.
gen-dafont-dogica-noto-serif: Chunky pixel-style swagger up top, then a literary text serif underneath with a gentle thick-and-thin cadence. Dogica's wide tracking against Noto Serif's tall lowercase is what the pair does best.
gen-dafont-dogica-sora: Sora reads precise and geometric, with curves that turn corners cleanly. Over a long page its parted c and s keep the text crisp, while Dogica's tall lowercase sits above it, heavy and wide.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-alpino: Early GameBoy brings open, stretched-out letters with a playful bark. It makes the best headline, while Alpino, tall and cozy with tightly packed spacing, does the quiet work of carrying the text.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads bookish and graceful, with wide channels into every counter. A long stretch of it moves smoothly, its modest weight shifts giving Early GameBoy's tall, commanding headings something gentle to land on.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-fs-roundo: Early GameBoy has a soft, slightly tilted-nib variation in its extended letters, a playful touch that stays commanding. Roundo takes over for reading, its neon-tube line thickness never shifting.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-sans-le: Early GameBoy stands out for its open, extended tracking and a faint upstroke-to-downstroke difference. And Noto Sans Lepcha supplies the sturdy counterweight, its wide-open curves and cast-iron stature making the pair approachable and firm.
gen-dafont-early-gameboy-gf-noto-sans-sy: Playful from the first line, Early GameBoy spreads wide. Noto Sans Syriac then reads easily over longer stretches, its tall bowls and wide, easy s turns keeping the text friendly and modern.
